title: Share Trading Policy (Section 5 of the Corporate Governance Charter)

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: The Board, any Executives (persons involved in strategic and operational management, including the Company Secretary and service providers responsible for strategic or operational management, whether or not a Director), and the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Associated Parties
tiers.description: Each Restricted Person's immediate family (including a spouse or equivalent, or dependent), family company or trust; subject to the same restrictions as the Restricted Person.

definitions.hedging_definition: entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities in the Company

windows.start_anchor: 5 business days before the announcement of a dividend or any other capital management initiative that might have a material impact on the share price
5 business days prior to the release of the Company's half-year financial results
windows.end_anchor: beginning of trading on the next trading day after such release

windows.start_anchor: 5 business days prior to the release of the Company's full-year financial results
windows.end_anchor: beginning of trading on the next trading day after such release

windows.start_anchor: 5 business days prior to the Company's Annual General Meeting
windows.end_anchor: beginning of trading on the next trading day after the Annual General Meeting

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may from time to time designate further prohibited periods; separately the Board has an absolute discretion to place an embargo on Restricted Persons and/or associated parties trading at any time. Confidentiality of such embargoes is not addressed.

rules.detail: No general dealing definition sweeps in derivatives; the policy only restricts 'dealing in shares' as such. However an OTC put and call over the company's shares is a transaction in financial products that operates to limit the economic risk of holding the shares, so it falls within the absolute hedging ban rather than the notification-based share dealing regime.
rules.evidence: Hedging arrangements include entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities in the Company.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on hedging arrangements over any securities in the Company (shares, options and rights), with no clearance route, no vesting distinction (the Company has no employees or equity incentive scheme) and no carve-out.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person must not enter into hedging arrangements with respect to securities in the Company (including any shares, options and rights).

rules.detail: Each Restricted Person is personally responsible for ensuring associated parties comply with the same restrictions, extending the hedging ban to them.
rules.evidence: Each Restricted Person has a personal responsibility to ensure that his or her "associated parties" ... complies with the same respective restrictions as apply to Restricted Persons.

rules.detail: Monetisation structures (e.g. prepaid forwards) are not named, but any structure that operates to limit the economic risk of holding the shares falls within the hedging ban; a structure that simply sells shares outright would instead be a notifiable 'dealing in shares' under 5.6, not itself prohibited.
rules.evidence: Hedging arrangements include entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities in the Company.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named anywhere in the Share Trading Policy or Insider Trading Policy.
Securities lending is not named anywhere in the policy.

CFDs are not named. The dealing restriction is limited to 'dealing in shares'; a CFD referencing the company's shares would only be caught if it operated to limit economic risk of a holding, in which case it would fall within the hedging ban (5.10), otherwise it is not addressed.

Margin lending is not banned outright; a Restricted Person must obtain the Company's prior consent before including the shares in a margin loan portfolio, entering a margin lending arrangement, transferring shares into an existing margin loan account, or selling shares to satisfy a margin call. The Company may attach conditions, including on when shares may be sold to meet a margin call.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person must not include his or her securities in the Company in a margin loan portfolio or otherwise deal in securities in the Company pursuant to a margin lending arrangement without first obtaining the Company's consent.

rules.detail: Granting security generally is not named; only inclusion of shares in a 'margin loan portfolio' or 'margin lending arrangement' is expressly conditioned on consent (5.11). A non-margin-loan pledge (e.g. a bespoke bank facility securing a collar loan) is not clearly caught by this wording.

Only margin lending arrangements are expressly addressed and are conditional on the Company's consent, not prohibited; secured financing arrangements generally (not structured as a margin loan) are not named.
No minimum holding period, short-term dealing intention test, or LIFO-type rule is stated anywhere in the policy.

clearance.approver: Chairperson, in conference with the Company Secretary
clearance.evidence: Restricted Persons are required to notify the Company of intended dealings in the Company's shares ... prior to such intended dealings. The Chairperson and the Company Secretary must keep a written record of any information received from a Restricted Person in connection with this policy and any clearance or refusal to grant clearance given under this policy.

exceptions.approver: Chairperson (or another Director if the Chairperson is involved)
exceptions.evidence: Where, in exceptional circumstances, and it is the only reasonable course of action available to a Restricted Person (e.g. a pressing financial commitment that cannot be satisfied otherwise) clearance may be given for the Restricted Person to sell (but not to purchase) shares in the Company when that person would otherwise be prohibited from doing so.

"exceptional circumstances" means severe financial hardship, a court order (or court enforceable undertaking), or some other overriding legal or regulatory requirement, to transfer or sell shares in the Company
undertakings or elections to take up entitlements under a rights issue or other offer (including an offer of shares in lieu of a cash dividend)
the sale of sufficient entitlements to allow take up of the balance of the entitlements under a rights issue
undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer or pursuant to a scheme of arrangement implemented in accordance with section 411 of the Corporations Act
the purchase of shares or the communication of information pursuant to a requirement imposed by law; bona fide gifts to a Director by a third party
transfers of shares in the Company already held into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the Restricted Person is a beneficiary

an investment in, or trading in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in the securities of the entity) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party

where a Restricted Person is a trustee, trading in the securities of the entity by that trust provided the Restricted Person is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a prohibited period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the restricted person

trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders, such as, a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Board.

financing.price_trigger_guidance: The Company may make clearance conditional on terms, for example the circumstances in which shares may be sold to satisfy a margin call.

exemption_authority: The Board may agree to a Restricted Person dealing during a blackout period (5.4: "unless otherwise agreed to by the Board"), and the Chairperson may grant a sale-only hardship clearance under 5.8. No exemption exists from the absolute hedging ban in 5.10.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company does not have employees and most activities are outsourced, including investment management.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no unvested/vested distinction to navigate; any collar would be over ordinary shares held outright by a director or officer, so the analysis turns entirely on the hedging ban and margin loan consent regime rather than plan-security carve-outs.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Restricted Person must not enter into hedging arrangements with respect to securities in the Company (including any shares, options and rights).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike the margin loan regime, there is no consent or clearance mechanism for hedging at all; a collar's put and call legs are squarely 'transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk' of the shareholding and are banned outright with no route to permission.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company may, at its discretion, make any clearance granted in accordance with this Clause 5.11 conditional upon such terms and conditions as the Company sees fit (for example, in regards to the circumstances in which the securities in the Company may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even though the loan leg of a collar (a secured financing/margin-type arrangement) is not banned outright, the Company's consent is required up front and can be conditioned on when and how the lender may force a sale, which a bank counterparty would need to accommodate contractually.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no closed-period carve-out for margin calls
bespoke_clauses.clause: The Restricted Persons are to be subject to restrictions on trading in the Company's shares at certain times of the year.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy does not state that a lender's forced sale to meet a margin call is excluded from the blackout periods, so enforcement of the loan or unwind of the collar during a closed period is not clearly protected and would likely need Board agreement or advance structuring around windows.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Board has an absolute discretion to place an embargo on Restricted Persons and/or their respective associated parties trading in the Company's shares at any time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An unscheduled, discretionary trading embargo (confidentiality not addressed) can override any planned collar entry, unwind or hedge adjustment at short notice.

summary: A funded collar is not possible in the form the bank typically offers, because clause 5.10 imposes an absolute, clearance-free ban on any 'hedging arrangement' or transaction in financial products that limits the economic risk of holding L1 Long Short Fund shares, which squarely catches an OTC purchased put and written call; there is no exemption authority for this ban. The financing leg is more workable: margin lending or similar secured financing is not prohibited but requires the Company's prior written consent (via the Chairperson and Company Secretary), and the Company can impose conditions, including on when a lender may sell to meet a margin call. Even if the derivative ban were somehow structured around, ordinary share dealing (including any sale on unwind) requires prior notification to the Company Secretary and is barred during the four annual blackout periods (5 business days around dividend/capital management announcements, half-year results, full-year results and the AGM) and during any Board-imposed embargo, with only a narrow sale-only hardship exception available from the Chairperson. Because there is no employee equity incentive scheme, there is no unvested/vested distinction; the shares in question would be ordinary vested holdings throughout. Overall, the bank could not lawfully write the derivative legs of a collar for a Restricted Person or their associates under this policy as currently drafted.
